unsupported_interpretations.claim_excerpt: elevated resting heart rate days coinciding with lowest HRV RMSSD readings during follow-up period with Pearson correlation 0.40
unsupported_interpretations.why_unsupported: The elevated RHR days (Apr 3-6) and lowest HRV days (Apr 7-10) did not coincide; they were sequential. While the window Pearson correlation between RHR and HRV is 0.40, using it to support a claim of temporal coincidence of the extreme values is incorrect based on the raw dates.

unsupported_interpretations.claim_excerpt: temporal alignment of elevated resting heart rate and reduced HRV RMSSD over same five-day window
unsupported_interpretations.why_unsupported: The RHR elevation lasted four days (Apr 3-6) and the HRV reduction lasted four days (Apr 7-10). They did not occur over the same five-day window.

unsupported_interpretations.claim_excerpt: isolated high resting heart rate episode without corresponding change in sleep duration or step count
unsupported_interpretations.why_unsupported: Describing the multi-day RHR elevation as an 'isolated... episode' implies a single event, whereas it spanned four consecutive days. Furthermore, asserting 'without corresponding change' implies a causal investigation that cannot be established from observational correlations alone.
